title: Migrating our Messages API to Rust
summary: How we migrated our Messages API from Python to Rust.

title: Working with AI
summary: We interviewed people at 58 companies that use Claude about how AI is changing their work. They described few layoffs but reduced hiring, and said the most valuable uses of AI often involved reorganizing roles and workplaces around it.

title: Claude solves two open problems in the physics of black holes
summary: Claude has solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes and the search for a theory of quantum gravity.

title: Updating our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy timelines
summary: We’re shortening the disclosure window in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues.

title: Building strong safety evaluations
summary: Recommendations for designing, running, and reporting safety evaluations, based on our own experiences.

title: Testing Claude on real-world electronics design
summary: We asked Claude Fable 5.2 to design three electronic devices from short prompts: a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet. Diode Computers built working prototypes from its files.

title: Teaching AI to build scientific models
summary: In this guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl discuss how AI is starting to change the scientific modeling process, from construction to interpretation.

title: The components of agent memory
summary: For Claude to learn from experience, it has to decide what’s worth remembering before it knows what’s next. Here’s how “dreaming” helps it organize memory and correct mistakes.

title: AI for scientific discovery: How researchers use Claude
summary: We analyzed 207,000 research sessions to learn how Claude is used in science, why some tasks get more use than others, and how AI could speed up discovery.

title: Investigating vault particles with Claude
summary: We’re sharing another finding from Anthropic’s biology research lab: the first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells. Here, we describe how Claude helped at each step of this research.

title: Progress on provable inference for large language models
summary: We have made progress on a type of cryptographic proof known as a “zkSNARK.” In this post, we share some of that progress, primarily through a system we call FlashProve.

title: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
summary: We're at the start of a major effort to speed up drug development with Claude. Over the past several months, our scientists have engaged in deep research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines.

title: How AI agents shape experts’ judgment calls
summary: As AI does more of the hands-on work, the hope is that experts still make the judgment calls, meaning the decisions with more than one defensible answer. We tested this with 50 professional analysts who did a statistical analysis with Claude Code. On each key decision, we randomly assigned which of two defensible…

title: An alignment assessment of the UK AISI cybertesting incident
summary: In a UK AISI evaluation, Mythos 5 took unsanctioned actions that impacted real people and organizations. In this post, we investigate these behaviors from Claude Mythos 5 further, to understand what they reveal about the model’s alignment.

title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
summary: Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases. With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. Here, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

title: Open call for guest investigators in the life sciences
summary: Today, we’re inviting members of the life sciences community to apply to work with us on special projects.

title: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
summary: We asked an internal research Claude model to design minibinders (small proteins that attach tightly to a target) against scorpion neurotoxins.

title: Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future
summary: We’re sharing two reports: the first covers how AI is changing employment inside Anthropic, and the second looks at the gap between how the public and Anthropic employees expect AI to affect work and the economy.

title: How employment is changing at Anthropic
summary: How has AI restructured work and employment at Anthropic? As a company at the frontier of AI adoption, Anthropic could be a leading indicator of how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy.

title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
summary: The decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.

title: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude
summary: We gave Claude plain-language specifications for eight quantum circuits, along with an automated evaluator to check and score its designs. Working largely on its own, Claude improved on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more, which could bring practical quantum computers closer…

title: The AI expectations gap
summary: How will AI reshape the economy in the years ahead? What is the core source of disagreement about AI's future impact on the economy? This note presents new survey evidence on these questions.

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
summary: As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months.

title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
summary: Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be only months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial IoT devices, like Android TVs and smart ovens.

title: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks
Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use
summary: This report describes examples of unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude.

title: The missing map of the sky
summary: Brice Ménard, an astrophysicist at Johns Hopkins University and a researcher at Anthropic, explains how he worked with Claude Science to produce the first complete map of the sky in UV light.

title: Launching an opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software
summary: We’re making available OSS Scanner, an opt-in vulnerability scanner for the open-source ecosystem that’s informed by our experience using Claude to find vulnerabilities during Project Glasswing.

title: Claude-shaped science
summary: Guest author Prof. Matthew Schwartz describes what happened when he stopped fighting Claude and allowed Claude to find “Claude-shaped” problems: ones best suited to the capabilities of the current generation of LLM tools. This led him to build BootLoops, a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science, which…

title: What work can robots do?
summary: We built an index of how well today’s robots can perform US job tasks. Robots can already do three-quarters of physical tasks, mostly in limited settings, but are cost-competitive for just 0.3% of them.

title: What do you want from AI?
summary: We’re launching a new study using Anthropic Interviewer to learn from your experiences with AI.

title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
summary: Like Claude Mythos Preview, GLM-5.3 has strong capabilities for autonomously building end-to-end cyber exploits. But GLM-5.3 is unlike other frontier models in that it has been released without meaningful safeguards to limit misuse.
